data.content_ref: inline:Target fails the critic school stance demanding a causal mechanism. It posits 'Non-Linear Temporal Friction' (time distribution per item) as the distinguishing evidence, but provides no causal mechanism explaining why temporal friction causes or constitutes a 'genuine reliability gain' rather than mere compliance. The temporal trace (spending disproportionate time) could easily be a symptom of confusion or inefficiency (as noted in its own counterconditions regarding inexperienced panels), yet the target asserts this observation directly distinguishes reliability without establishing the causal link required by the stance.
